lines.japanese: 「あのー、そういえばー」
lines.english: “Um, come to think of it...”

lines.japanese: 並んで歩くホーメイが、俺の頭から爪先まで、首を何度も上下させて眺めまわしている。
lines.english: Walking beside me, Phoenixsong bobbed her head up and down as she inspected me from head to toe.

lines.japanese: 「ドラさんって、工事現場のひとだったんですねー。へー、あんなところで何してお仕事に決まってますよねー」
lines.english: “Dora, so you work construction. Huh. What were you doing in a place like that—working, obviously.”

lines.japanese: 質問の途中で自己解決。答えかけていた俺は、アホみたいに口を開けたままになってしまった。
lines.english: She answered her own question halfway through asking it. I’d already opened my mouth to answer and was left standing there like an idiot.

lines.japanese: 「あらー、この服、ポケットいっぱい付いてますねー。うはー、お菓子とか入れ放題じゃないですかー」
lines.english: “Oh, this outfit has so many pockets. Wow, you could fill them with all the candy you wanted.”

lines.japanese: 落ち着きのない小娘は、俺の作業着や手に提げた安全帽がよほど珍しいらしい。首を伸ばして顔を近づけてくる。
lines.english: The restless girl apparently found my work clothes and the hard hat in my hand endlessly fascinating. She craned her neck and brought her face closer.

lines.japanese: 「おい。おい女。あんまじろじろ見んじゃねーよ、穴とか開いちゃうだろ」
lines.english: “Hey. Hey, woman. Quit staring. You're going to wear holes in me.”

lines.japanese: ホーメイは逃走を断念したあとでも、結局はじっとしていないやつだった。しかし、いまどきのギャルらしさに乏しいせいか、よく喋るわりにはそれほど騒がしいという印象がない。
lines.english: Even after giving up on escape, Phoenixsong remained incapable of sitting still. Yet perhaps because she lacked the flashy air of most girls her age, all her chatter never made her seem especially loud.

lines.japanese: 香田がきゃんきゃん鳴きながらしがみついてくる小型犬だとすれば、こいつはふんふん鼻を鳴らしてまとわりつくハムスターかフェレットだ。
lines.english: If Koda was a little dog that latched onto you yapping, this one was a hamster or ferret that followed you around snuffling.

lines.japanese: 鬱陶しいには変わりないけど、どっちの方がマシかって言えば──森里には悪いが、まあ、俺にはハムスターだ。
lines.english: They were both annoying, but if I had to say which was better—sorry, Morisato—I’d take the hamster.

lines.japanese: 「ほぁー、なんかー、ドラさんいまだけは働く男って感じしますねー」
lines.english: “Ooh. Just for this moment, Dora, you look like a working man.”

lines.japanese: 小娘はガラにもなく胸の前で十本の指を絡みあわせて、憧れの王子様を眺める村娘のような目で俺を見上げた──いや、どちらかと言えば、村の若者に恋してしまったお姫様か。
lines.english: In an entirely uncharacteristic display of demureness, the girl laced all ten fingers before her chest and gazed up at me like a village maiden beholding her prince. No—more like a princess who had fallen for a village boy.

lines.japanese: 「はー、こういうのも『馬子にも衣装』って言うんでしょうかー」
lines.english: “Oh. Is this what they mean by ‘even a stable hand looks good in the right clothes’?”

lines.japanese: しかしビミョーに感じ悪い。
lines.english: And yet it sounded faintly insulting.

lines.japanese: 「っせえな、見るなっつってんだよ」
lines.english: “Shut up. I told you not to look.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、すみません、こんな間近で見るのは初めてなもので。やーでも、意外にかっちょよいですねー、ほどよく汚れた作業着。くはー」
lines.english: “Ah, sorry. I've never seen work clothes this close before. But they're unexpectedly cool, aren't they? Just the right amount of dirt. Whew.”

lines.japanese: そう言いながら、やつは俺の体に鼻を近づけてくんくんさせる。
lines.english: As she spoke, she brought her nose close to me and sniffed.

lines.japanese: ハムスター……。
lines.english: Hamster...

lines.japanese: 「おい。おいおまえ。俺が格好いいのは分かるけど、俺ほら、ハードボイルドだから。あんま惚れんじゃねーぞ。火傷とかすんぞ」
lines.english: “Hey. Hey, you. I know I’m good-looking, but see, I’m hard-boiled. Don’t go falling too hard for me. You’ll get burned.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、それはまったく心配ないと思います」
lines.english: “Oh, I don't think there's the slightest danger of that.”

lines.japanese: やつは作業着の縫い合わせを眺めながら、憎たらしいぐらいあっさり言いきった。
lines.english: Still studying the seams of my work clothes, she dismissed the possibility with infuriating ease.

lines.japanese: しかし、そのあとで俺の顔を見上げ……一回大きな瞬きをしてから「あれ？」と首を傾げた。
lines.english: But then she looked up at my face, gave one enormous blink, and tilted her head. ‘Huh?’

lines.japanese: 「なんだよ」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「えー、おかしーなー、ドラさんってイケメンのひとでしたっけー？」
lines.english: “How strange. Dora, were you always handsome?”

lines.japanese: 目と口を真ん丸くしたアホ面で、ぽかんと呆けている。
lines.english: Her eyes and mouth formed perfect circles. She stared in witless astonishment.

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　なに今更なこと聞いてんだよ。そうに決まってんだろ」
lines.english: “What? Why ask something so obvious now? Of course I was.”

lines.japanese: 「いやー、そんなはずないですよー。ただの無愛想な『しけたつら』じゃないですかー」
lines.english: “No, that can't be right. Don't you just have a sullen, dreary face?”

lines.japanese: 「なんだ。なんだコレ。ケンカ売られてんのか俺」
lines.english: “What is this? Are you picking a fight with me?”

lines.japanese: 「おっかしーなー、なんでいまキュンってなったんだろー」
lines.english: “How strange. Why did my heart just go *thump*?”

lines.japanese: 「この胸の高鳴り……もしかして恋の予感？」
lines.english: “This pounding in my breast... Could it be the first stirring of love?”
“Ueegh!?”

lines.japanese: 小娘が瞳を伏せて頬に手を添えた。俺は泣きそうになった。
lines.english: The girl lowered her eyes and laid one hand upon her cheek. I nearly burst into tears.

lines.japanese: 「まー、たぶん、なにかの間違いだと思いますけどねー」
lines.english: “Well, it's probably some kind of mistake.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、そうだろ。ぜってーそうだって。おまえ、風邪でもひいたんじゃね？」
lines.english: “Obviously. Definitely. Maybe you're coming down with a cold?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、それかあれですねー。私、こんな風に普通に話せるひとがあまりいないんで、ＴＰＯを踏まえない魂がびっくりして勘違いを起こしてしまったんですねー」
lines.english: “Yes, or perhaps it's this. I don't have many people I can talk to normally, so that habit of mine with no sense of time, place, or occasion got startled and mistook the feeling for something else.”

lines.japanese: 「それだ」
lines.english: “That's it.”

lines.japanese: 言ってる意味はよく分からなかったけど、とりあえず同意した。
lines.english: I had no real idea what she meant, but I agreed anyway.

lines.japanese: 「あとはー、ドラさんが制服姿の女の子に一方ならぬ情熱を持っていたようにー、私もワークウェア姿の男のひとに潜在的な嗜好心を持っていたのかもしれませんねー」
lines.english: “Or perhaps, just as you harbor an extraordinary passion for girls in school uniforms, I have a latent preference for men in work clothes.”

lines.japanese: 「あのさ、おまえそれ、どこまで冗談で言ってんの。返答によっちゃ出るとこ出るけど。名誉毀損とかで」
lines.english: “How much of that is supposed to be a joke? Depending on your answer, we may be settling this in court. Defamation and all that.”

lines.japanese: 「そうかー、私、作業着フェチだったのかー」
lines.english: “I see. So I have a work-clothes fetish.”

lines.japanese: 「おい。おい女。キモい独り言つぶやきながら顔近づけんな。あと口閉じろ口。よだれ垂れんぞ」
lines.english: “Hey. Woman. Don't bring your face closer while muttering creepy things to yourself. And close your mouth. You're about to drool.”

lines.japanese: 「あのー、ちょっと生地、触ってみていいですかー」
lines.english: “Um, may I touch the fabric?”

lines.japanese: 「よくねーよ。オプション料金とんぞ」
lines.english: “No. That option costs extra.”

lines.japanese: しかし女は俺が答えるより早く、袖の布地を擦りあわせるように摘みあげていた。
lines.english: But before I could answer, she had already pinched the cloth of my sleeve and begun rubbing it between her fingers.

lines.japanese: 「うわー、すごーい、ふつー」
lines.english: “Wow. Amazing. Completely ordinary.”

lines.japanese: 「っせーな、普通に決まってんだろ。綿１００パーなめんなコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Shut up. Of course it's ordinary. Don't underestimate one hundred percent cotton, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 腕を振りぬき小娘を引きはがす。やつは俺から離れて、ひとり腕を組んだ。
lines.english: I whipped my arm away and shook the girl loose. Once separated from me, she folded her arms and considered the matter.

lines.japanese: 「うーん、でも今度はときめかないなー、原因は作業着じゃそういえばドラさんって、建築会社にお勤めのひとなんですか？」
lines.english: “Hmm, but my heart didn't flutter that time. So the work clothes aren't the cause—oh, come to think of it, Dora, do you work for a construction company?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、プー」
lines.english: “No. Unemployed.”

lines.japanese: いいかげんこいつの唐突な話題転換には慣れてきたので、今度はすぐに答えられた。
lines.english: By now I was accustomed to her abrupt changes of subject, so this time I answered at once.

lines.japanese: 「本業は学生さんですか？」
lines.english: “Is being a student your main occupation?”

lines.japanese: 「本業がプー」
lines.english: “Unemployment is my main occupation.”

lines.japanese: 「就職はしないんですか？」
lines.english: “Don't you intend to find a job?”

lines.japanese: 「就職はできないんです」
lines.english: “I can’t find one.”

lines.japanese: 「前科何犯なんですか？」
lines.english: “How many prior convictions do you have?”

lines.japanese: 「なんでだよ」
lines.english: “Where did that come from?”

lines.japanese: 「馬鹿、違げっつーの、そーゆーこっちゃねんだよ。アレだよ、不景気なんだよ。日本中のお父さんが就職難なんだよ。てめ、２１世紀の失業率なめんなコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Idiot, that's not it. Nothing like that. It's the economy. Fathers all over Japan can't find work. Don't underestimate twenty-first-century unemployment, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 「はー、ちゃんとバランスの取れた食生活できてますー？」
lines.english: “Are you managing to eat a balanced diet?”

lines.japanese: 「っせーな」
lines.english: “Shut up.”

lines.japanese: 「国民年金は払ってますかー？」
lines.english: “Do you pay into the national pension?”

lines.japanese: 「うるせーっつうの。なんだてめえは。区役所か。興信所か。俺のマニアか」
lines.english: “I said shut up. What are you, the ward office? A private investigator? President of my fan club?”

lines.japanese: 「あー！　ドラさんちょっとヘルメット見せてください！」
lines.english: “Oh! Dora, please let me see your helmet!”

lines.japanese: 「ちょーちょー、おま、どんだけ自由なんだよ。自由過ぎんだろ。少しはひとの話も聞いてくんない」
lines.english: “Whoa, whoa—you seriously just do whatever you want, don’t you? Could you listen when someone else is talking once in a while?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、聞いてますよー」
lines.english: “Yes, I'm listening.”

lines.japanese: 「でも私ー、自分に都合悪かったり答えにくかったりする質問だと、聞いてても聞いてないふりするんですよー」
lines.english: “But when a question is inconvenient for me or difficult to answer, I pretend I didn't hear it.”

lines.japanese: 「ですよーじゃねーだろ、てめ、マジかよ」
lines.english: “Don't say it as though that makes it fine. Are you serious?”

lines.japanese: 「すごーい、ヘルメット超きいろー」
lines.english: “Wow. This helmet is incredibly yellow.”

lines.japanese: 「うわ、マジだ」
lines.english: “Whoa. It really is.”

lines.japanese: ホーメイは勝手に俺の手から安全帽をひったくり、矯めつ眇めつ眺めまわした。
lines.english: Phoenixsong snatched the hard hat from my hand without permission and examined it from every angle.

lines.japanese: 「あのー、ちょっとこれ、かぶってみてもいいですかー」
lines.english: “Um, may I try this on?”

lines.japanese: しかし「いいですか」の「で」の辺りで、すでに頭半分が黄色い半球に埋もれている。人の返事を待たない女だ。
lines.english: But by the time she reached the word *may*, half her head had already disappeared into the yellow hemisphere. This woman never waited for an answer.

lines.japanese: 「べつに被んのはいーけど、おまえソレ、臭ぇから嗅ぐなよ」
lines.english: “Wear it if you want, but it stinks, so don't sniff it.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、はい、もちろんです」
lines.english: “Ah, yes. Of course.”

lines.japanese: やつは失礼な了解をしながら、しかしなぜかメットを脱いで、その内側をわざわざ鼻先へ持ってゆく。
lines.english: She acknowledged the warning with insulting readiness, then for some reason removed the helmet and deliberately raised its interior to her nose.

lines.japanese: 次の瞬間──
lines.english: The next instant—

lines.japanese: 「っっっっっっ！」
──それは勢いよく俺に突きかえされた。
lines.english: —she thrust it violently back at me.

lines.japanese: 「アホか。だから、ひとの忠告は聞いとけっつーの」
lines.english: “Idiot. That's why you listen when somebody warns you.”

lines.japanese: こいつ、いつか無意識の好奇心で身を滅ぼしそうだ。
lines.english: One day, heedless curiosity was going to be the death of her.

lines.japanese: 両手で鼻腔をふさぎ悶絶する女。
lines.english: She writhed with both hands clamped over her nostrils.

lines.japanese: 「……いや、ちょっと待て。いくらなんでもそこまでは臭くねーだろ」
lines.english: “...Wait a minute. It can't possibly smell *that* bad.”

lines.japanese: 「はー、思わず化学の実験で使ったカルボン酸を思いだしてしまいました」
lines.english: “Whew. It reminded me of the carboxylic acid we used in chemistry class.”

lines.japanese: 「仕方ねーだろ、それだけ汗かく仕事なんだよ」
lines.english: “Can't be helped. It's the kind of job that makes you sweat.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、これじゃ百年の恋も冷めてしまいますねー。世の中には大変なお仕事があったものです」
lines.english: “Yes. A smell like this could kill a lifelong love in an instant. My, what difficult professions the world contains.”

lines.japanese: いやな理解の示し方だった。
lines.english: That was an unpleasant way to show understanding.

lines.japanese: 「ドラさん、それちゃんと洗ってるんですかー？」
lines.english: “Dora, do you ever wash that thing?”

lines.japanese: 「メットは洗わねーだろフツー」
lines.english: “People don't normally wash helmets.”

lines.japanese: 「そうなんですかー？」
lines.english: “They don't?”

lines.japanese: 「たぶん……え、だって洗濯機入んねーじゃん」
lines.english: “Probably... I mean, it wouldn't fit in the washing machine.”

lines.japanese: 俺は適当なことを言ってまた歩きはじめた。やつも慌てて踏みだし横に並ぶ。
lines.english: I gave her an offhand answer and started walking again. She hurried to catch up and fell into step beside me.

lines.japanese: ──と思ったら、すぐにまた一歩だけ下がって立ちどまる。どうやら首を伸ばして、銀行の裏口の自転車置場を覗いているみたいだった。
lines.english: —or so I thought. She immediately dropped back one step and stopped. Apparently she was craning her neck to inspect the bicycle rack behind a bank.

lines.japanese: 「ないなー」
lines.english: “Not there.”

lines.japanese: なんとなく俺は、その独り言を聞かなかったことにした。
lines.english: For some reason, I pretended not to hear the murmur.

lines.japanese: 「なあ。おまえ、終電間に合うんだろうな」
lines.english: “Hey. You're going to make the last train, right?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、はい、大丈夫のはずです。まー、いざとなれば、一時間ぐらいかかるけど歩けない距離でもありませんしー」
lines.english: “Oh, yes. I should be fine. And if it comes to that, it would take about an hour, but it isn't too far to walk.”

lines.japanese: 「あきらめんな。徒歩禁止」
lines.english: “Don't give up already. No walking.”

lines.japanese: 「とほー」
lines.english: “On foot? What a de-feet.”

lines.japanese: 黙って歩きつづける。くだらない駄洒落は文字通り屁みたいなもんだ。つまり聞こえなかったことにしてやるのが礼儀。
lines.english: I continued walking in silence. A lousy pun was literally like a fart: etiquette required pretending you had not heard it.

lines.japanese: 「えー、あれー、ツッコミいただけないんですかー」
lines.english: “What? I don't even get a retort?”

lines.japanese: 「それが優しさってもんだろ」
lines.english: “That's what kindness means.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、ドラさんツッコミのひとじゃないですかー。さっき左右田さんたちに、いっぱいつっこんでたじゃないですかー」
lines.english: “But Dora, you're the one who fires back. You had an answer for everything Mr. Souda and the others said.”

lines.japanese: 「ひとを漫才師みたいに言うんじゃねーよ。あんなん反論してただけだっつの」
lines.english: “Don't make me sound like half of a comedy duo. I was only arguing with them.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、でも見事なツッコミでしたよー。言われたことないですかー」
lines.english: “But they were splendid comebacks. Has nobody ever told you that?”

lines.japanese: あったような、なかったような。俺は答えなかった。
lines.english: Maybe someone had. Maybe nobody had. I did not answer.

lines.japanese: 歩いているうち、視界にきらびやかなサインボードが一つずつ増えてきた。自分の靴音が聞こえなくなるぐらいには喧騒も近付いている。
lines.english: As we walked, glittering signboards appeared one by one. The din drew close enough to swallow the sound of my footsteps.

lines.japanese: 「ちょおー、もーう、待ってくださいよーう」
lines.english: “Heyyy, come onnn, wait for meee.”

lines.japanese: ホーメイの呼びかけで、俺は自分の歩くペースが速まっていることを知った。
lines.english: Phoenixsong's call made me realize that my pace had quickened.

lines.japanese: 「ドラさんはレディに対する気遣いがなってないですよう」
lines.english: “Dora, you show no consideration for a lady.”

lines.japanese: 「っせえなあ」
lines.english: “Shut up.”

lines.japanese: 英語はよく知らないけど、おまえの見てくれはガールの範疇じゃないのかと思った。しかし相手が本気で気にしてることだったら悪いので、口にはしなかった。
lines.english: I didn't know much English, but judging by her appearance, I would have placed her in the category of *girl*. If the distinction genuinely mattered to her, saying so would be cruel, so I kept it to myself.

lines.japanese: いちおう俺でも、そのぐらいの気遣いはできるんだ。
lines.english: Even I could manage that much consideration.

lines.japanese: 「おや。また来たのかい」
lines.english: “Oh? You've come again.”

lines.japanese: いま思いだしてみても、じいさんの声は礼拝堂の祭壇みたいに厳かで、ステンドグラスから差しこむ昼下がりの陽光みたいに柔らかだった。
lines.english: Even now, the old man’s voice remains in my memory: solemn as a chapel altar and gentle as afternoon sunlight through stained glass.

lines.japanese: 説教壇の上に横たえていた体を、俺はことさら重たげに起こしてみせた。
lines.english: I made a show of laboriously hauling myself upright from where I lay sprawled across the pulpit.

lines.japanese: 「んだよ、来ちゃ悪りーのかよ」
lines.english: “What? Is it bad that I came?”

lines.japanese: 声変わりすら迎えてないくせに精一杯つっぱってたガキを、じいさんはどんな風に思ってたんだろう。
lines.english: My voice hadn't even broken, yet I strained with all my might to act tough. I wonder what the old man thought of that child.

lines.japanese: 「構わんさ。心に雨の降る日は、ここで祈って虹を待ちなさい。私はいつでも歓迎するよ」
lines.english: “Not at all. On days when rain falls in your heart, pray here and wait for the rainbow. You are always welcome.”

lines.japanese: 「ただし、椅子と机を間違えない子供に限るがね」
lines.english: “Provided you’re a child who can tell a chair from a desk.”

lines.japanese: 「っせーなあ、こっちのが座り心地いいんだよ」
lines.english: “Shut up. This one's more comfortable.”

lines.japanese: 俺は悪びれない素振りで鼻筋に深いしわを刻んだあと、尻を載せていた檀上から飛びおりた。窓の外──階下の庭からは、呑気な子供たちのはしゃぎ声が聞こえた。
lines.english: I wrinkled my nose deeply, showing no hint of remorse, then jumped down from the platform where I had been sitting. Beyond the windows—from the garden below—came the carefree cries of children at play.

lines.japanese: 住宅地の中ほどにあるその小さな教会は、平日の午後になると、一階の集会所や遊戯室を地域の住民に開放していた。心に鍵をぶらさげた子供たちは、そこで夕暮れまで時間を潰して親の帰りを待つ。
lines.english: The little church stood in the middle of a residential neighborhood. On weekday afternoons it opened its ground-floor meeting hall and playroom to local residents. Children with house keys hanging over their hearts spent the hours there until dusk, waiting for their parents to come home.

lines.japanese: なんたら子どもクラブ、とかいう名前だったと思うけど、要は学童保育ってやつだったんだろう。
lines.english: I think it was called the Something-or-Other Children's Club. In other words, after-school care.

lines.japanese: 俺はガキのころから集団行動が苦手だったから、よく指導員のおばちゃんの目を盗んでは階段を上がって礼拝室へ忍び込んだものだった。
lines.english: Group activities had never suited me, even as a child. I often slipped away while the women supervising us were not looking, climbed the stairs, and snuck into the chapel.

lines.japanese: おばちゃんたちに見つかると、もちろんこっぴどく叱られた。しかし、ひと目で本職の聖職者と分かる厳粛な雰囲気をまとったあのじいさんだけはいつも、祈りに来たのであれば咎めはしないと言って俺を赦した。
lines.english: Naturally, the women supervising us scolded me mercilessly whenever they caught me. But the old man alone—visibly a real clergyman, with all that solemn dignity—always forgave me. If I had come to pray, he said, there was nothing to condemn.

lines.japanese: いまなら分かる。じいさんはきっと、賑やかな遊戯室から逃げだしてきたはぐれ者の立場と心情を理解していたんだろう。
lines.english: Now I understand. The old man must have known what it was like to be the outcast who fled the noisy playroom.

lines.japanese: 「なあ、いいからはやく稽古つけてよ」
lines.english: “Come on. Enough of that. Start teaching me.”

lines.japanese: 習ったばかりの構えをとって、握ったこぶしを数回、前に繰りだす。脇を浮かすな、という基本は忘れちゃいない。下半身のステップワークだって、形だけは様になってたはずだ。
lines.english: I took the stance I had only just learned and drove my clenched fists forward several times. I had not forgotten the basic rule about keeping my elbows in. Even my footwork must have looked reasonably convincing, at least in outline.

lines.japanese: 「ふむふむ」
lines.english: “Hmm, hmm.”

lines.japanese: じいさんは一丁前の闘志を見せるガキに優しく微笑んだ。若いころそこそこ名の知れた拳闘家だったと言う大柄な聖職者は、もう還暦を迎えたにも関わらず背筋一つ曲がっていなかった。
lines.english: The old man smiled gently at the boy mustering a grown man’s fighting spirit. He was a large clergyman who claimed to have been a boxer of some renown in his youth, and even at sixty he stood perfectly straight.

lines.japanese: 「お祈りは済んだのかい」
lines.english: “Have you finished your prayers?”

lines.japanese: 「だからいつも言ってんじゃん、俺そーゆーの信じないんだって」
lines.english: “I tell you every time. I don't believe in that stuff.”

lines.japanese: じいさんが脇に抱えていた分厚い本を、俺は小さな人差し指で示す。やつは呆れたようにまぶたを閉ざすと、素早く十字を切った。
lines.english: With one small index finger, I pointed at the thick book tucked beneath his arm. He closed his eyes in exasperation and swiftly crossed himself.

lines.japanese: 「信仰は無理強いしないけどね……ええと、君は隼人君と言ったかな。君にはまず、心を落ちつけるすべを身につけてもらいたいんだ」
lines.english: “I won't force faith on you... Let me see, your name was Hayato, wasn't it? Before anything else, I want you to learn how to calm your heart.”

lines.japanese: 「でなければこれ以上は教えられない。分かるかい。強い体を育むには、同時にそれを抑えられる強い心を育てなければならないんだ」
lines.english: “Otherwise I can teach you no more. Do you understand? If you build a strong body, you must also build a heart strong enough to restrain it.”

lines.japanese: そしてじいさんは、さほど広くもないホールの中央に立ち、いかにも聖職者くさい微笑を満面に湛えた。
lines.english: Then the old man stood in the center of the modest hall, his whole face filled with the sort of smile only a clergyman could wear.

lines.japanese: 「さあ坊や、祈りなさい」
lines.english: “Now, child. Pray.”

lines.japanese: 俺は見つめられる窮屈さから逃れるように、長椅子（うるさいから机はやめておいた）の一端に腰を落としてふんぞりかえった。
lines.english: To escape the discomfort of being watched, I dropped onto one end of a pew—I’d left the desk alone because he would not shut up about it—and sprawled back.

lines.japanese: 「んーだよ、あんたいまシンコーは強要しねーつったばっかじゃん」
lines.english: “What the hell? You just said you wouldn't force your faith on me.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そうか……んんっ、ごほん、なに、神様に祈らなくてもいいんだ。目を閉じて、心を開き、内なる自分に向かいあうだけでいい。ここはそういう場所だ。さあ、出来るだろう、祈りなさい」
lines.english: “Ah, yes... Ahem. You needn't pray to God. Simply close your eyes, open your heart, and face the self within. That is what this place is for. Come, you can manage that. Pray.”

lines.japanese: 「やっぱ強要じゃん。なあ、シンコーの自由とかって、ホーリツで決まってんじゃなかったっけ」
lines.english: “That’s still forcing me. Isn’t freedom of religion guaranteed by law?”
“Ha ha...”

lines.japanese: じいさんは苦笑いを浮かべながら、その大きな手で後ろ頭をがしがしと掻く。
lines.english: With a rueful smile, the old man scratched vigorously at the back of his head with one enormous hand.

lines.japanese: 「いや、参ったな。屁理屈こねないでくれよ、坊主」
lines.english: “You have me there. Don't split every hair, little preacher.”

lines.japanese: 「坊主はあんただろ」
lines.english: “You're the preacher.”

lines.japanese: じいさんは一瞬目を丸くしたけれど、すぐに破顔して肩をすくめた。
lines.english: The old man's eyes widened for an instant. Then his face broke into a smile, and he shrugged.

lines.japanese: 「はは、君は揚げ足とりが上手だな。でも言葉から棘は抜いた方がいい。せっかくの愉快な個性が台無しだ」
lines.english: “Ha ha. You’re very good at catching people out on their own words. But you should pull the thorns from yours. They spoil that delightful personality of yours.”

lines.japanese: 皺だらけのくせして妙に若々しい顔が、俺の目線に合わせてそっと下りてきた。
lines.english: His strangely youthful face, for all its wrinkles, lowered gently to the level of my eyes.

lines.japanese: 「隼人君。もしそれが出来るようになれば──神様に誓ってもいい──いまはひとりでも、いつか君のもとにはきっとたくさんのお友達が集まるようになる」
lines.english: “Hayato. If you learn to do that—I swear before God—then although you may be alone now, one day a great many friends will surely gather around you.”

lines.japanese: 「はん、くだらねー。べつにいらねーし、そんなん」
lines.english: “Hah. Stupid. I don't want anything like that.”

lines.japanese: 「いまはそう思っていてもね、いつかは必ず欲しくなるときが来るのさ。まったく不都合なことに、残念ながら人間っていうのはそういう風にできているんだ」
lines.english: “You may think so now, but the day will surely come when you do. Regrettably—and most inconveniently—that is simply how human beings are made.”
